obernants.scope: U consists of (build, environment history, texts, tagged Ok/Error/Exit outcome). R selects the latched mode and executes its pipeline. U minus R includes successful truncated returns after worker panic, successful GPU dispatch in a CPU-only build, and switching mode after a valid latch. Resource aborts and parser quality are outside this bound.
For Ok word batches y, R^-1(y) contains all texts and parser states mapping to y, with input count equal to output count. Casing, ambiguity and approximate GPU outputs prevent unique text recovery.
For pure f, positive cap and completed jobs, y[i]=f(x[i]); joining and flattening follow source slice order regardless of completion order.
All spawned handles are joined before Result collection; any join panic produces Err. Already completed side effects survive. Public par_map converts Err into a panic.
Let t=min(available_parallelism or 4,cap)>0 and c=max(ceil(n/t),1). Worker count is ceil(n/c) for n>0 and zero otherwise. cap=0 is outside the helper model.
Empty OnceLock takes the first accepted environment mode; later environment edits cannot change that stored mode. GPU requires a feature-enabled build.
Before a mode latch, exit(2) corresponds to a Unicode value other than cpu/gpu or gpu without feature. Missing or non-Unicode environment lookup errors choose CPU.
With the same annotator and no worker panic, CPU result is the sequence Tree::parse_cased(a,text).w. This says nothing about parse correctness or GPU agreement.
GPU success requires predicted sentence count equal to nonempty-token inputs and per-sentence token count equality; scatter preserves original empty sentence positions.
Unknown tags fall back to NN; relations try full label, then pre-colon base, then Dep. Distinct raw labels may therefore yield identical completed outputs.
GPU OnceLock stores the first Result of model load; failed initialization remains failure even after changing model path. Annotator acquisition precedes cache lookup.
GPU finish repairs when WORLD_NO_REPAIR lookup errors, then lowercases form and lemma. Compatible input fibers include alternative case and pre-repair structures; switch is read per finish.
